$comment: Ratified PATH entries that scripts\consolidate-path.ps1 -Prune may remove. DATA, not code, for the same reason config\sysmon-filedelete.xml is: the list is a judgement somebody made on one particular day and has to be reviewable without reading PowerShell. Every 'require' predicate is RE-MEASURED at run time by Get-PathHygienePlan (lib\ShimPlan.ps1); an entry whose precondition no longer holds is SKIPPED and reported, never removed. Entries are written with %VAR% where one exists so the file is not specific to this box: the expanded value is what gets MATCHED, and the raw registry literal is what gets REMOVED. %USERPROFILE% is safe to expand even in the elevated child, because consolidate-path.ps1 refuses to run when the elevated SID differs from the SID that asked (see its -ElevatedFor guard) - so the profile cannot belong to a different administrator.

entries.reason: Present in BOTH hives, so the user copy contributes nothing to resolution - Windows composes machine-then-user and the machine copy answers first. Removing the machine copy instead would be wrong: some shells inherit the machine PATH only, which is the failure this script was written for.
Same cross-scope duplicate. ollama.exe keeps resolving from the machine entry.
Same cross-scope duplicate. Literal rather than %VAR%-based because C:\Anthropic is a managed install root with no environment variable pointing at it.

The toolbox's own entry, in BOTH hives since install-machine-scope.ps1 ratified the machine copy: bootstrap.ps1 added the user copy on every run because Add-UserPathEntry only ever looked at the user hive. Machine composes first, so the user copy has never won a lookup and removing it cannot change which ffmpeg or rg answers. Add-UserPathEntry now checks the machine hive before adding, so a -Prune here is not undone by the next bootstrap run - if that guard ever regresses the two would fight over the hive forever, which is why Invoke-InstallerTests asserts its order and its return.
Same duplicate, same cause, same guard. procdump, handle and sigcheck keep resolving from the machine copy.

Zero executables: the directory was emptied by the 2026-09-10 wipe and nothing has re-populated it. A dotnet global tool install would put one back, which is why the predicate is re-measured instead of trusted - the entry earns its place again the moment it holds a tool.

Provides pip, pip3 and pip3.11. pip and pip3 already resolve to C:\Anthropic\.Python3\Scripts, which is PATH entry 3 and therefore wins today; only the version-pinned pip3.11 alias is lost, and it is declared here so the removal is a stated trade rather than a surprise in the resolution delta. Paired with the entry below to de-shadow the compliance-visible 3.11 interpreter.

Provides python and pythonw, both of which already resolve to C:\Anthropic\.Python3 at PATH entry 4. Taking it off PATH is the point rather than a side effect: a 3.11 interpreter reachable as bare 'python' is what trips compliance scanners, which is the same rule smoke-test.ps1 enforces for the toolbox venv Scripts directory.

Provides java, javac, javaw and jshell, every one of which already resolves to the Eclipse Adoptium jdk-21 bin directory at PATH entry 1. Oracle's javapath is a directory of symlinks to whatever the last Oracle JRE installer decided; it wins nothing here and is a second, invisible answer to 'which java'.
